response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT arcref, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scanqc GROUP BY arcref), s AS (SELECT arcref, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), d AS (SELECT arcref, cnt, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS deviation FROM s), r AS (SELECT arcref, cnt, share, deviation, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY deviation DESC) AS rnk FROM d) SELECT arcref, cnt AS qc_count, share, deviation FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY deviation DESC

assumptions.assumption: Projects are the distinct arcref values present in scanqc. Projects with no QC records are excluded, so the average share is 1 divided by the number of projects in scanqc.

'10th-highest deviation' is the deviation of the 10th row in descending order, counting tied rows as separate rows. RANK() <= 10 returns every row whose deviation is at least that value. If fewer than 10 projects exist, all are returned.
